english: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=\dfrac{x^{3}+x}{5}$. If $f^{-1}$ is the inverse function of $f$, then the total area of the regions enclosed between the curves $y=f(x)$ and $y=f^{-1}(x)$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\dfrac{x^{3}+x}{5}$ द्वारा परिभाषित है। यदि $f^{-1}$, $f$ का प्रतिलोम फलन है, तो वक्रों $y=f(x)$ तथा $y=f^{-1}(x)$ के बीच घिरे क्षेत्रों का कुल क्षेत्रफल ______ है।
solution: $f'(x)=\dfrac{3x^{2}+1}{5}>0$ and $f$ is onto $\mathbb{R}$, so $f^{-1}$ exists; its graph is the mirror image of $y=f(x)$ in $y=x$
$f$ increasing $\Rightarrow$ the curves meet only on $y=x$: $\dfrac{x^{3}+x}{5}=x\Rightarrow x=0,\pm2$
On $(0,2)$: $x-f(x)=\dfrac{4x-x^{3}}{5}>0$, so $f$ is below $y=x$ and $f^{-1}$ above; each loop is bisected by $y=x$
$f$ is odd, so the loop on $[-2,0]$ has the same area
solution_full: $f'(x)=\dfrac{3x^{2}+1}{5}>0$ for all $x$, so $f$ is strictly increasing; as a cubic with positive leading coefficient it is onto $\mathbb{R}$. Hence $f^{-1}:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ exists, and the graph of $y=f^{-1}(x)$ is the reflection of the graph of $y=f(x)$ in the line $y=x$.

For a strictly increasing $f$, if $f(a)=f^{-1}(a)=b$ then $f(b)=a$; $a<b$ would give $f(a)<f(b)$, i.e. $b<a$, and similarly $a>b$ is impossible. So the curves meet only on $y=x$, where $\dfrac{x^{3}+x}{5}=x$, i.e. $x^{3}-4x=0$, $x=-2,0,2$.

On $(0,2)$: $x-f(x)=\dfrac{4x-x^{3}}{5}=\dfrac{x(2-x)(2+x)}{5}>0$, so $y=f(x)$ lies below $y=x$ and, by reflection, $y=f^{-1}(x)$ lies above it. The loop between the curves over $[0,2]$ is symmetric about $y=x$, so its area is twice the area between $y=x$ and $y=f(x)$.

$\displaystyle\int_{0}^{2}\left(x-\dfrac{x^{3}+x}{5}\right)dx=\dfrac15\int_{0}^{2}\left(4x-x^{3}\right)dx=\dfrac15\left(8-4\right)=\dfrac45$, so this loop has area $\dfrac85$. (No formula for $f^{-1}$ is needed.)
$f$ is odd, so $f^{-1}$ is odd as well, and the whole picture is symmetric about the origin: the loop over $[-2,0]$ also has area $\dfrac85$.
Total area $=\dfrac85+\dfrac85=\dfrac{16}{5}=3.2$. (Numerical integration of $\left|f(x)-f^{-1}(x)\right|$ over $[-2,2]$ also gives $3.2$.)
originality_note: New: two loops, symmetric about the origin, between an odd increasing cubic and its inverse, whose inverse has no usable closed form, so the symmetry about y = x and the oddness both have to be used (way 4). Closest known: area between y = x^3 (or x + sin x) and its inverse in the first quadrant. Different because: the student must first show that the curves meet only on y = x, find both loops and use oddness for the second one.
stem_review: Read as a student: every set, function and symbol introduced with its domain, conditions complete, one reading of each sentence; answer recomputed with code and unique; answer matches the plan. Checked that 'regions enclosed between the curves' means both bounded loops (over [-2,0] and [0,2]) and that there are no others (the curves meet only at -2, 0, 2); numerical integration with mpmath of |f - f^{-1}| gives 3.2. Changed: No change.
key_step: Using reflection in y = x: the area between f and f^{-1} is twice the area between f and y = x, after showing the curves meet only on y = x.
justification: Two ideas linked (meeting points of an increasing function and its inverse lie on y = x; area doubled by symmetry) plus oddness for the second loop; the computation is light. Comparable to 2026-P2-Q18 (L3), an area found by a symmetry argument.
blueprint_concepts: Inverse of a function: existence, graph symmetry about y = x
Area bounded by a curve and its inverse

concept_use.Inverse of a function: existence, graph: f is strictly increasing and onto, so f^{-1} exists and its graph is the reflection of y = f(x) in y = x; the curves therefore meet only on y = x, at x = 0 and x = ±2.
concept_use.Area bounded by a curve and its inverse: The area between y = f(x) and y = f^{-1}(x) is computed as twice the area between y = f(x) and y = x on each loop, giving 8/5 + 8/5.
